title: SDK flow: fidelity trading & atomic tool handles (PRD draft)
content:
Status: draft - sketching a developer-facing surface that gives apps deterministic latency budgets, a small set of fidelity knobs, and a compact primitive for durable/atomic tool interactions.

Summary:
This PRD drafts a combined API and SDK pattern we call "atomic tool handles" paired with a "fidelity trading" model for streaming responses. The goal is to let client apps deliberately trade token-level latency vs. result fidelity while maintaining simple, restartable tool-call semantics and strong observability. This is intended for high-throughput hosted API customers integrating tools (search, DB lookup, action execution) into streaming LLM responses.

Problem we solve:
- Current streaming responses blur tool boundaries: clients either buffer full tool outputs or accept partial, inconsistent results during mid-stream tool calls.
- Developers need predictable latency SLOs for UI flows (e.g., search-as-you-type) while still wanting high-quality structured outputs when they can wait a bit longer.
- Tool-call semantics are fragile across network retries and client disconnects—lack a compact durable primitive that is easy to reason about in SDKs.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Provide an SDK surface that exposes a small latency/fidelity API: Low, Medium, High fidelity choices with clear expected token-latency ranges and quality tradeoffs.
- Define an "atomic tool handle": an idempotent, resumable reference a model can return while streaming so clients can resolve tool-side actions deterministically after reconnects or retries.
- Streaming behavior guarantees: progressive tokens that can be displayed, plus checkpoints that mark tool-handshake boundaries.
- Observability: per-request fidelity setting, tool-handle lifecycle events, and end-to-end time-to-first-usable-output metrics captured in Redwood Console.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not define new model architectures or training requirements for tool-aware decoding. It is an API & SDK ergonomics layer.
- Not covering dedicated/private deployment differences; focus is hosted API UX and SDK ergonomics.

User scenarios:
1) Search preview (low latency): product search UI sends a streaming request with fidelity=low. Model returns fast, concise answers; tool handles point to lightweight search result references (summary only). UI updates as tokens arrive.
2) Assisted composition (medium fidelity): editor asks for structured JSON with citations. Model streams partial text, emits a tool-handle when it invokes a citation lookup; client can show placeholders until the handle resolves.
3) Transactional action (high fidelity): agent orchestrator invokes external DB update through a tool; model requests confirmation and returns an atomic tool handle which the client must resolve to execute the action.

Key primitives and semantics:
- fidelity: one of [low, medium, high] (string token). SDK exposes this as an enum and maps to internal decoding profiles (batch-size, kv-cache warmup aggressiveness, sampling temperature). Expectation docs will list median TTF token ranges per cloud region and model family.

- atomic_tool_handle (string id):
  - Returned inline as a JSON frame during streaming, e.g. {"frame":"tool_handle","id":"th_123","tool":"vector_search","spec":{"q_sig":"sha256:..."}}
  - Semantics: identifies a durable reference that can be resolved by the client against Redwood’s tool resolution API or the customer-provided callback on private deployments.
  - Guarantees: idempotent resolution (resolve multiple times => single side-effect) when created with resolution_mode="at-most-once-confirmed" or best-effort for read-only handles.
  - Lifecycle: CREATED -> RESOLUTION_REQUESTED -> RESOLVED/FAILED. SDK surfaces lifecycle events and exposes a promise-like handle for app code.

- stream_checkpoint (optional): periodic stable markers emitted by the service indicating a consistent prefix that survived model fallback/rollouts. Clients can use these for local replay or snapshotting session state.

Streaming contract (high-level):
- Frame types: text_token, structured_chunk, tool_handle, checkpoint, end_of_stream, error. Each frame is newline-delimited JSON for backwards compatibility with existing streaming SDKs.
- Client side: SDK exposes a tap/observable that yields frames in order. For text_token frames clients may render immediately. For tool_handle frames the SDK returns an "AtomicToolHandle" object with methods: resolve(options), status(), on(event, cb).
- Reconnects: when reconnecting to a session id, SDK will request last_checkpoint; server rewinds to checkpoint and resumes streaming. Any tool handles created before checkpoint are considered durable; handles created after may be retried or rolled back depending on resolution_mode.

Fidelity trading (how apps use it):
- Low: optimized for first-byte latency. Uses aggressive prefix cache hits and smaller decode batches. Expected median time-to-first-token reduced by ~30% vs. medium. Output is focused and more extractive.
- Medium: balanced; good for general chat and structured output where occasional re-ranking is acceptable.
- High: emphasize completeness and citation/format correctness. Larger decode batches and more conservative kernel selection; higher per-token cost and latency.
- SDK UX: a single call option fidelity="medium" and a "fidelity_hint" string for more granular tradeoffs (e.g., "prioritize-citations").

Atomic tool handles detailed behavior and patterns:
- Use case: model initiates a calendar booking flow. Instead of requesting the client to immediately call an external endpoint, model emits a tool_handle with a payload containing the normalized action parameters and a confidence score. The client can inspect, optionally confirm with the user, then call handle.resolve({confirm:true}).
- Guarantee matrix: resolution_mode options: at-most-once-confirmed (server ensures single execution), best-effort (may execute multiple times on retries), dry-run (no side-effect, returns simulated result).
- Security: handles may be signed JWTs indicating creation time and expiration. SDK enforces TTL and warns if resolving expired handles.

SDK ergonomics and code snippets (sketch):
- JS streaming flow:
  const stream = client.streamCreate({model: 'rwd-2.1-stream', fidelity: 'low'});
  stream.on('text_token', t => renderToken(t));
  stream.on('tool_handle', h => { const th = new AtomicToolHandle(h); showPlaceholder(th.id); th.on('resolved', r => replacePlaceholder(r)); });
  await stream.done();

- AtomicToolHandle.resolve() returns a promise that follows the lifecycle. SDK retries on transient network errors and surfaces resolution_id for tracing.

Observability and metrics:
- Emit fidelity tag on every request metric.
- Tool handle metrics: created_count, resolve_attempts, resolve_success_rate, avg_time_to_resolve.
- Console traces should link stream frames to token-level logs and tool resolution events so engineers can replay problematic sessions.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Alpha (internal + 3 verified customers): implement frame types, SDK preview, Console instrumentation. Collect TTF and resolution latencies. (6 weeks)
- Beta (wider partners): add fidelity profiles for top 5 models, add at-most-once-confirmed mode. (8 weeks)
- GA: full docs, JS/TS/Python SDKs, SLAs updated for transactional handles. (6 weeks)

Milestones & owner:
- API frame spec v0 (owner: Maya) - 2025-02-28
- JS SDK prototype (owner: Ethan) - 2025-03-14
- Console metrics plumbing (owner: Priya) - 2025-03-21
- Alpha customers onboarding (owner: Samir) - 2025-04-11

Open questions / risks:
- Do we need additional fidelity tiers for very low-latency mobile cases?
- How to represent complex tool payloads compactly without leaking PII in logs? Need schema/hints for redaction.
- Idempotency: can backend guarantee at-most-once for all third-party tools? May need connector-level confirmations.

Appendix: example frames (newline delimited):
{"frame":"text_token","data":"The top results are"}
{"frame":"tool_handle","id":"th_123","tool":"vector_search","spec":{"q_sig":"sha256:abcd"},"resolution_mode":"best-effort"}
{"frame":"checkpoint","cursor":"ck_20250210_a1"}
{"frame":"structured_chunk","schema":"receipt.v1","data":"{...}"}

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus review on the atomic tool handle lifecycle and expected semantics for resolution_mode.
- Provide input on fidelity profiles for rwd-2.x model family: what are realistic median token TTF windows we should publish?

References: internal chat threads (see linked_artifacts), related PRDs on progressive output and stream checkpoints.

-- Maya Patel
